Selected Story
A single, generic addition to the Narrative user prompt—an extra section titled “Preserve Editorial Intent from the Synthesis”—coincided with consistent editorial drift in three candidate runs: Nuëyon’s company identity and audience scope were subordinated, orchestration was elevated to the central message, and unsupported audience/validation language appeared. The experiment changed only that one prompt file, produced measurable declines in Narrative and Compose scores compared with baseline, and led to the candidate prompt being rejected and the production prompt restored. The reader should understand that, in this controlled test, one narrowly scoped prompt change produced reproducible regressions in editorial outcomes and was not promoted; the results show a clear signal in these runs but do not establish broader causality or generality.

Story Progression
- Context: Explain the audience (prompt engineers, workflow owners, content-product and editorial ops managers) and the specific intervention—a single, generic “Preserve Editorial Intent from the Synthesis” section added to Narrative.user.prompt.txt while all other inputs and prompt files remained identical.
- Development: Present the concrete observations that make the shift tangible: only the user prompt text changed; Narrative mean score fell from 6.00 to 4.00 and Compose mean fell from 5.67 to 3.33; all three candidate Narrative and Compose runs failed the acceptance gates that kept orchestration as a supporting explanation and that enforced factual/editorial restraint; and candidate outputs consistently demoted company identity, elevated orchestration, and added unsupported audience/validation claims (example: Compose run 3 reframed content creation as an orchestration/architecture problem).
- Endpoint: Close with the supported outcome—because the candidate prompt produced consistent regressions under the experiment’s acceptance criteria, the candidate was rejected and the production Narrative prompt was rolled back; the results indicate a reproducible signal in this test but do not prove mechanism or broad generality.

Critical Constraints
- Do not attribute the prompt change’s effect to a specific cause or actor; state only that the single prompt file changed and the observed outputs followed.
- Do not invent or imply a team, collective decision-maker, or who approved or executed the rollback beyond the documented outcome that the candidate was not promoted and production was restored.
- Do not claim causal mechanisms (e.g., wording, placement, model seed, temperature, or backend) unless supported by additional evidence; treat the mechanism as unknown.
- Do not generalize the experiment’s result beyond the tested runs: do not present the outcome as a broad proof that all similar guardrails will fail or succeed.
- Do not present the supplied example(s) as proof of mechanism—use them only as observed outputs that make the drift concrete.
